title: Protected Charge and Price-Protection Excess: Billing Calculation for Cartwise Grocery Orders
content:
# Price-protection refund on a replacement line

Cartwise Grocery Orders — billing calculation. The price-protection refund concerns a replacement line whose substitution decision is automatic best match and whose billed unit price is above the original unit price by more than the substitution price cap percentage of the order's service level; on any other line the refund is nothing. It is worked from the replacement line's billed entry: the billed units, the billed unit price, the original unit price of the product originally ordered, and the line's billed charge.

## Calculation

(a) The **protected unit price** is the original unit price multiplied by one plus the service level's substitution price cap percentage divided by 100.

(b) The **protected charge** is the billed units multiplied by the protected unit price, rounded to the cent.

(c) The **price-protection excess** is the line's billed charge less the protected charge, never below zero.

(d) The **price-protection refund** is the price-protection excess, rounded to the cent, and never more than the line's billed charge.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Inputs chosen for illustration only: original unit price 3.00, replacement billed at 3.90 a unit for 2 units, line charge 7.80, on a service level whose substitution price cap is taken, for the example, as 20 percent.

- The line qualifies: 3.90 is above 3.00 by more than 20 percent (the cap figure is 3.60).
- Protected unit price: 3.00 multiplied by 1.20 gives 3.60.
- Protected charge: 2 multiplied by 3.60 gives 7.20.
- Excess: 7.80 less 7.20 gives 0.60.
- Refund: 0.60.

## Boundary cases on the same hypothetical line

| Replacement billed unit price | Above the original by more than the cap | Refund |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3.60 (exactly at the cap) | no | nothing |
| 3.61 | yes | 0.02 (charge 7.22 less protected charge 7.20) |
| 3.90 | yes | 0.60 |
